plan.title: WT vs KO drug response: 2x2 interaction DE + enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question — does the drug act differently in KO than in WT — is a genotype x treatment interaction question by definition, and the data (12000 genes x 16 samples used for the design, 4 replicates per cell of a 2x2 genotype[WT,KO] x treatment[vehicle,drug] factorial, salmon-derived raw integer counts) supports exactly that test. The plan follows the DESeq2 interaction workflow end to end: (1) QC on variance-stabilized data to confirm the four groups separate and no sample is an outlier before any test is fit; (2) minimal low-count pre-filtering appropriate for n=4 per cell; (3) a single DESeq2 negative-binomial model with design ~genotype+treatment+genotype:treatment, explicit reference levels (WT, vehicle); (4) the interaction coefficient (genotypeKO.treatmentdrug) tested first as the direct answer to 'does the drug effect differ by genotype', with ashr-shrunken log2FC since it is a single named coefficient but reported alongside the two simple effects (drug vs vehicle within WT; drug vs vehicle within KO) built as combined coefficient contrasts, per DESeq2's own interaction vignette guidance; (5) BH FDR at alpha 0.05 per contrast, independent filtering on; (6) GO biological-process over-representation (clusterProfiler enrichGO, tested-genes-as-universe, rrvgo redundancy collapse) run separately for each of the three gene lists (interaction, WT simple effect, KO simple effect) — this is the enrichment method the design knowledge service actually permits for a 4-replicates-per-cell design; a Reactome/WikiPathways lookup against the local pathway GMTs supplements interpretation of any hits; (7) a consolidated report giving the three-way table (WT effect / KO effect / interaction) DESeq2's own documentation requires for an interaction design, with MA/dispersion diagnostics, leading-edge-equivalent gene tables, and full session info. Power to detect the interaction term itself is explicitly flagged as low at n=4/cell — a difference-of-differences with n=4 has limited power, and the report states this rather than treating a null interaction as evidence of 'no difference'.
